summary: Independent GRAVEYARD red-team pass challenged all 12 active-batch theses for hidden concentration, capital intensity, policy exposure, dilution, backlog quality, substitution and execution traps. No thesis is falsified outright. The most important common failure mode is correlated dependence on hyperscaler AI capex and constrained infrastructure: a single regime reversal can hit semiconductor compute, custom silicon, foundry, memory, networking and power/cooling names simultaneously. Several companies still require normalized customer/backlog/capital-structure evidence before Chief promotion.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Record backlog and acquisitions can mask schedule, cancellation, integration and cash-consumption risk. The announced Iridium transaction plus Neutron increase execution surface area before the launch economics of Neutron are proven.
contradictions: Revenue/backlog growth is real, but scale does not prove backlog quality or post-acquisition return on capital.
unknowns: Backlog cancellation rights, acquisition funding bridge, exact Neutron cash need and milestone slippage sensitivity.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Material cancellations, repeated Neutron delays, or integration costs rising faster than gross-profit generation.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: End-customer concentration is extreme: 32%, 33% and 19% for three end-customer profiles in FY2026. Architecture or procurement changes at one hyperscaler can create an abrupt demand cliff despite strong current margins.
contradictions: Exceptional growth and profitability coexist with concentrated demand and bargaining power.
unknowns: Duration and pricing protections of major programs; normalized SBC dilution and true customer diversification after contract-manufacturer pass-through.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Subsequent filings show durable end-customer diversification without gross-margin erosion.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Rapid Scorpio ramp can create product/program concentration, inventory risk and expectations fragility. High gross margin and growth reduce solvency concern but can obscure dependence on a narrow set of AI platform designs.
contradictions: Q2 revenue of $392.4M and strong gross profit demonstrate execution, but do not establish independent customer breadth.
unknowns: End-customer concentration, fully diluted share-count roll-forward and cancellation/return exposure on major product ramps.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Scorpio adoption broadens across independent buyers with stable margins and no material inventory/cancellation build.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: One direct customer represented 16% of Q2 revenue and management still flags direct/indirect concentration. China remains structurally constrained by licensing, inspection and tariff rules, which also encourage domestic substitutes and custom accelerators.
contradictions: Platform dominance and demand remain extraordinary while concentration/policy risk is also unusually high in absolute dollars.
unknowns: Incremental hyperscaler custom-silicon substitution, sovereign restrictions beyond China, and normalized capital-return dilution after SBC/buybacks.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Customer concentration falls materially while software ecosystem share and gross margin remain resilient against custom accelerators.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Data Center is now 58% of revenue, increasing dependence on EPYC/Instinct execution. The same export regime that hurt MI308 creates inventory/licensing uncertainty, while software and customer concentration can limit accelerator economics.
contradictions: Data Center revenue more than doubled, but scale does not prove durable share or peer-level accelerator margin.
unknowns: Instinct end-customer concentration, repeat-order breadth and normalized accelerator gross margin.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Broad multi-customer MI-series repeat deployments with improving margins and software adoption.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Q3 AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B and Q4 guidance of $21.7B create enormous sensitivity to a small number of custom-accelerator programs. Prior filings show one semiconductor distributor at 42% of revenue and top-five end customers near 45%; VMware adds integration/debt history even as FCF is strong.
contradictions: 46% FCF margin is a major buffer, but cash generation does not eliminate hyperscaler bargaining power or program concentration.
unknowns: Customer-level AI mix, program cancellation protections and exact debt/deleveraging trajectory.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI custom programs broaden materially across independent customers while debt declines and margins remain durable.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: 77% of wafer revenue is 7nm-and-below, increasing dependence on leading-edge demand and very high capex. Geographic diversification reduces tail risk but may duplicate fixed costs and learning curves; Taiwan remains a physical concentration point.
contradictions: 2nm ramp and 67.7% gross margin demonstrate process leadership while overseas replication can pressure normalized economics.
unknowns: Customer concentration, overseas-fab margin drag and capex intensity after current AI buildout normalizes.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Overseas fabs reach comparable yields/economics and customer concentration declines without margin sacrifice.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: EUV scarcity is powerful but concentrated customer capex and export policy can make bookings lumpy. Management expected China sales to decline significantly in 2026; High-NA technical success still requires customer ROI and utilization to justify adoption pace.
contradictions: €38.8B backlog and 50%+ gross margins support pricing power while policy and fab-cycle timing remain outside ASML control.
unknowns: Current China mix, key supplier single-source dependencies and production-scale High-NA utilization economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: High-NA adoption broadens on schedule and China decline is absorbed without backlog/margin volatility.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top-five customers are about 57% of revenue, Arm China about 16%, and SoftBank-linked commercial arrangements are material. Related-party/control dependence plus RISC-V and proprietary architectures complicate the apparent resilience of an asset-light model.
contradictions: Very high gross margins and ecosystem reach are durable strengths but do not remove governance/customer concentration.
unknowns: Related-party economics, independent data-center royalty mix and long-run RISC-V substitution rate.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Royalty growth broadens across independent data-center customers while SoftBank/Arm China dependence falls materially.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Q3 revenue of $41.46B and gross margins above 80% in several units are extraordinary for memory and therefore vulnerable to supply response and mean reversion. Record capex is necessary to capture HBM demand but can become destructive if competitors close yield/capacity gaps.
contradictions: Strategic customer agreements improve visibility while memory remains a historically supply-responsive industry.
unknowns: Take-or-pay/floor economics, competitor HBM4 yields and capex/debt normalization across the next downcycle.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: HBM scarcity and contract economics sustain margins through significant competitor capacity additions.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: First $3B quarter and strong margins can obscure cloud-titan concentration and architecture risk. Hyperscalers can internalize software/hardware or shift to proprietary fabrics; 1.6T adoption must broaden beyond a few marquee customers.
contradictions: Broad growth and platform innovation are strong, but strategic concentration is more important than financing risk.
unknowns: Current top-two customer share, attach rates across independent buyers and white-box/custom-network substitution pace.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: 1.6T adoption broadens while customer concentration declines and margins stay resilient.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Vertiv explicitly warns that orders can be cancelled and backlog may not convert. AI data-center power/cooling scarcity can induce double-ordering while grid/interconnection delays push projects out, creating a mismatch between reported backlog and realized timing.
contradictions: Strong execution and demand support the scarcity thesis, but backlog quality is not equivalent to contracted cash flow.
unknowns: Backlog aging/cancellation terms, hyperscale customer concentration and project deferral sensitivity to power availability.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with low cancellations through a broad customer base despite grid delays.

materialFindings.finding: The active batch has material common-shock concentration: NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, ALAB, TSM, ASML, MU, ANET and VRT all depend to varying degrees on the same AI-infrastructure investment regime.
CRDO remains the sharpest quantified customer-concentration risk in the batch; AVGO and ARM also disclose material concentration, while NVDA's latest quarter identifies a 16% direct customer.

Backlog/order strength for RKLB and VRT must remain discounted until cancellation, aging and schedule quality are normalized; both businesses face project-execution pathways that can make headline backlog overstate realized timing.

contradictions: Record growth across the batch can be genuine and still represent one correlated macro bet rather than diversified evidence.
Asset-light or high-margin models at ARM, CRDO and NVDA still carry concentrated-customer and policy dependence that gross-margin optics can obscure.
unknowns: Comparable end-customer concentration is unavailable for several names because disclosures differ between direct customers, distributors and true end customers.
Current backlog cancellation/aging terms remain incomplete for RKLB and VRT.
Normalized diluted share-count/SBC overhang remains incomplete for several high-growth semiconductor names.

peerRequests.request: Close comparable end-customer concentration for CRDO/ALAB/NVDA/AMD/AVGO/ANET and diluted-share normalization before promotion.
Stress one broad AI-capex slowdown through foundry, memory, interconnect, networking and power/cooling transmission paths.
Treat record growth and backlog as high-expectation states unless reproducible valuation evidence shows adequate asymmetry.

accuracyDebates.reason: Nominal ticker diversification materially overstates economic diversification in this active batch.
Backlog without cancellation/aging/schedule evidence can inflate confidence in RKLB and VRT.
